title: Acoustic dose-response plate design with constant DMSO backfill
summary: A design pattern for Echo-based dose-response experiments: compounds sit in Echo-qualified source plates, each dose is transferred in multiples of the 2.5 nL drop, and DMSO is backfilled so every well carries the same solvent load; controls are added per plate and well positions can be randomised.

steps.text: Define the source plate map: well, compound and stock concentration, in Echo-qualified 384PP or 384LDV plates.
Plan a nine-point dose-response layout where each transfer volume is rounded to a multiple of 2.5 nL.
Add DMSO backfill so total DMSO per well is constant (about 100 nL in the example).
Acoustically transfer compound doses into the destination plate.

duration_s.note: Per-plate time not stated in source; 2-5 min per plate from docs/pipelines.md planning figure.

steps.text: Add vehicle and positive controls on every plate.
Optionally randomise destination wells and keep replicates far apart to limit positional bias.

source.authors: Kattunga V.M., Wrobel S.A., Lerner C.A. et al.

notes: Preprint (not peer reviewed). Source does not say which Echo model; echo_650 is our assumption.
